expected_segments: In a busy street, a small change can create a new conflict: a door opens, someone steps around a parked van, or a bus prepares to leave. Good driving leaves room for those changes.

In this chapter M05-L01 · See the person behind the movement M05-L02 · When the street changes purpose M05-L03 · Choose a lawful place to stop M05-L04 · Manoeuvre where people may appear M05-R · Review and self-assessment Answers and review guidance Official references This material is a learning aid to help you understand Swedish driving theory. It is not an official source and cannot replace official information from Trafikverket and Transportstyrelsen. Always consult their current guidance and the applicable rules.

Arrival: 10:00. Schematic timeline - not to scale 09:00 10:00 12:00 18:00 Two hours The two-hour limit is reached at 12:00. Check all other conditions before leaving the car. Your goal: Anticipate the needs of different road users without assuming that everyone sees, hears or moves as you do.

Requirements. Show particular consideration for children, older people, school patrols and people whose disability or illness is apparent and affects their use of traffic. Reduce speed appropriately near children, stopped passenger transport and other situations with foreseeable risks. Give pedestrians sufficient room and time when meeting or passing them. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §§15 and 58

Learning approach. Look for the space a person needs, not only the space they occupy now. A child may be hidden by a parked car. A cyclist may need to move out from an obstruction. A wheelchair user may need a usable kerb transition. You cannot reliably infer someone's hearing, vision or intentions from a quick glance. Allow time and observe their movement rather than demanding a response through the horn.
Observe people and possible movement Children, cyclists and riders have different needs. Sensory-impairment panels are separate examples; absence of a sign does not prove absence of risk.
People often cross, walk on or remain near this stretch of road. Allow for someone entering your path. Adult and child inside a warning triangle.
Pedestrians ahead. Adult and child inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
Children often cross or remain near this stretch. The sign supplies a warning, not a numerical speed limit. Two children inside a warning triangle.
Children ahead. Two children inside a warning triangle.
Cyclists or moped riders often cross or enter the road here. Cyclist inside a warning triangle.
Cyclists and moped riders ahead. Cyclist inside a warning triangle.
Sensory-impairment panels
People with impaired vision commonly use the area. Give them time and space without assuming they have seen you. Five black dots arranged horizontally on yellow.
People with impaired vision. Five black dots arranged horizontally on yellow.
Continue the learning
People with impaired hearing commonly use the area. Do not assume a horn will be heard. Three black dots inside a black circle on yellow.
People with impaired hearing. Three black dots inside a black circle on yellow.

Horses and riders also belong in your traffic assessment. Vehicle rules apply to riding and leading horses in relevant respects; they are not simply pedestrians because they travel slowly. Give them an unhurried, spacious interaction, and avoid unnecessary noise. This is a cautious application of the general duty of care, not a fixed passing-distance rule. Transportstyrelsen: horses in traffic
Horses and riders This warning supports early observation. It does not specify a fixed passing distance.
Riders often cross or use this stretch of road. Prepare for an unhurried, spacious encounter. Horse and rider inside a warning triangle.
Horse riders ahead. Horse and rider inside a warning triangle.

Bus rule. Where the maximum permitted speed is 50 km/h or lower, a driver approaching a bus whose driver signals to leave a bus stop must slow and give it the opportunity to leave, stopping if needed. The bus driver must also take particular care. If passing on the right of a bus or tram stopped at a stop without a refuge, stop to allow boarding or alighting passengers free passage. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§45 and 58
Recognise a bus stop and speed limit The bus-stop marker and the 40 km/h speed sign are independent examples. The bus marker itself does not set the speed limit.
This identifies a stop for scheduled services and school transport. Keep the stopping area available and watch for passengers. White bus on a blue rectangular sign.
Bus stop. White bus on a blue rectangular sign.
Do not exceed the displayed speed in km/h. A junction alone does not necessarily end the limit, and conditions may require a lower speed. Red-bordered yellow circle displaying 40: maximum 40 km/h.
Maximum speed. Red-bordered yellow circle displaying 40: maximum 40 km/h.
Share the space

Bus comparison · Check the road limit. The threshold concerns the maximum permitted speed on the road, not how fast you happen to be travelling. At a 70 km/h limit, the special bus-stop departure rule above does not apply. The bus must wait for an entry that can be made without danger or unnecessary obstruction. You still have a duty to adapt speed to facilitate an observed entry into your lane. A bus indicator does not create unconditional priority, and the higher road limit does not excuse deliberately blocking it. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§43–45
Road limit
Duties when the bus signals to leave its stop
50 km/h or lower
Slow and let the bus leave; stop if needed. The bus driver must take particular care.
70 km/h, ordinary entry into your lane
The special bus-exit duty does not apply. The bus waits for a safe entry; you adapt speed to facilitate the observed entry.

Safety advice · Let a guide dog work. Do not pet, call to or talk to a working guide dog to attract its attention. Distraction can endanger the person it is helping. Allow the pair room and time; if you need to communicate, address the handler rather than trying to direct the dog. The handler chooses the route and remains in control. For example, a passenger beside your parked car wants to greet a guide dog at a crossing. Ask them to leave it working and keep the path clear. MFD: meeting a working guide dog

Traffic terminology · A bicycle is a vehicle. A person riding an ordinary pedal bicycle is operating a vehicle, even without an engine. “Vehicle” does not mean only “motor vehicle”. Apply the relevant cyclist duties and protections; crossing distinctions remain in M04-L03. Transportstyrelsen: bicycle definition
Leave room for the bus and people

The bus signals to leave its stop. The full-width middle lane remains separate from the opposing lane. In the worked decision the road limit is 40 km/h; available road width does not remove the bus duty.

Worked decision. On a 40 km/h street, a bus signals out. You ease speed early and leave room rather than trying to squeeze past. You also watch for people near the stop; making space for the bus is not your only task. Compare an otherwise ordinary 70 km/h road: the bus waits for a safe entry, while you still adapt speed to help an observed entry into your lane. Travelling at 40 on that 70 road does not activate the special bus rule.
Check your understanding

Knowledge check. (1) Does a narrow visible gap beside a cyclist prove passing is safe? (2) A bus signals from its stop on a 70 km/h road while you drive at 40. Does the special bus rule apply, and what must both drivers do? (3) Should you greet a working guide dog? (4) Is a person riding a pedal bicycle operating a vehicle?
Remember: Predict possible needs without assuming a person will behave exactly as expected.
Your goal: Distinguish ordinary streets from pedestrian streets, walking-speed areas and cycle streets.

Requirements. On a pedestrian street (gågata) and in a walking-speed area (gångfartsområde), drive no faster than walking pace and yield to pedestrians. The general rule prohibits parking; a specifically signed lawful parking arrangement must be assessed on its own terms. Walking pace is a condition to match, not a universal speedometer number. Special streets · Traffic Regulation, chapter 8 §1 and chapter 10 §1
Pedestrian streets and walking-speed areas Two matched start/end pairs. Pedestrian-street access limits differ from walking-speed-area rules. Pedestrian street

Special pedestrian-street rules apply, including walking pace and yielding to pedestrians. Motor access is restricted to the permitted purposes; it is not a general shortcut. Adult and child within a blue rectangular sign.
Pedestrian street. Adult and child within a blue rectangular sign.
Continue the learning
The pedestrian street ends. Reassess the rules before entering another road. Pedestrian-street symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
End of pedestrian street. Pedestrian-street symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
Walking-speed area

Drive at walking pace and yield to pedestrians. Parking is generally prohibited except where a lawful signed arrangement provides otherwise. Street scene with pedestrians, a car, houses and a playing child.
Walking-speed area. Street scene with pedestrians, a car, houses and a playing child.
The walking-speed area ends. Leaving it does not give you priority over the road you enter. Walking-speed street scene crossed by a red diagonal.
End of walking-speed area. Walking-speed street scene crossed by a red diagonal.
Continue the learning

Motor vehicles may use a pedestrian street only to cross it, apart from the specified necessary journeys: goods to or from shops or equivalent premises; goods or residents to or from addresses there; guests to or from hotels or equivalent premises; and sick people or people with mobility impairments to or from an address. A convenient shortcut does not qualify. Check additional signs and local restrictions. Traffic Regulation, chapter 8 §1

On a cycle street (cykelgata), the maximum is 30 km/h, and motor vehicles must adapt speed to bicycle traffic. Vehicles entering from another road yield to vehicles already on it. Parking is restricted to specially provided places. When leaving a cycle street for another road, the exit yielding rule applies. Special streets · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §21 and chapter 8 §1a
Cycle streets Matched beginning and ending signs. Retain the entry and exit yielding duties in the lesson.
The maximum is 30 km/h and motor vehicles must adapt to bicycle traffic. Apply the cycle-street entry, exit and parking rules too. Bicycle with a smaller car above it on blue.
Cycle street. Bicycle with a smaller car above it on blue.
The cycle street ends. Apply the yielding rule when leaving it for another road. Cycle-street bicycle and car crossed by a red diagonal.
End of cycle street. Cycle-street bicycle and car crossed by a red diagonal.
Continue the learning

Learning approach. A change in street function changes your expectations. People may use more of the width; a car's arrival should not force them into hurried avoidance. Read the beginning and ending signs and identify whether your proposed journey is permitted before entering.
Check before entering
At a pedestrian-street boundary, the official E7 sign identifies the street’s purpose. Check whether your journey is permitted before entering; a navigation shortcut is not an exemption.
Worked decision. Your navigation suggests a pedestrian street as a shortcut. You continue to another permitted route. The navigation suggestion does not establish an exemption from the access rule.

Check access before choosing a route Independent examples of access prohibitions, paths, reserved lanes and no-through roads. These are not all installed at the illustrated pedestrian street. Access prohibitions
Vehicles must not enter from this direction. Do not confuse this with a prohibition applying in both directions. Red circle with a horizontal yellow bar.
No entry. Red circle with a horizontal yellow bar.
Vehicle traffic is prohibited. Read any applicable supplementary qualifications. Yellow circle with a red border.
No vehicles. Yellow circle with a red border.
Motor vehicles are prohibited, with class II mopeds excluded unless a panel also prohibits them. Car and motorcycle crossed by a red diagonal.
No motor vehicles except class II mopeds. Car and motorcycle crossed by a red diagonal.
Paths and reserved lanes
This is a designated cycle path. A supplementary panel states if class II mopeds are excluded. White bicycle on blue.
Cycle path. White bicycle on blue.
This path is intended only for pedestrians. White adult and child on blue.
Pedestrian path. White adult and child on blue.
Pedestrians and cyclists share the path. Read any panel excluding class II mopeds. Pedestrian and bicycle symbols share a blue circle without a dividing line.
Shared pedestrian and cycle path. Pedestrian and bicycle symbols share a blue circle without a dividing line.
The symbol positions identify each group's side. The paths are separated by a marking, strip or similar division. Pedestrians on the left and bicycles on the right, separated by a vertical line.
Separated pedestrian and cycle paths. Pedestrians on the left and bicycles on the right, separated by a vertical line.
Continue the learning
The symbol positions identify each group's side. The paths are separated by a marking, strip or similar division. Bicycles on the left and pedestrians on the right, separated by a vertical line.
Separated pedestrian and cycle paths. Bicycles on the left and pedestrians on the right, separated by a vertical line.
Do not assume an ordinary car may enter. Certain other users are permitted by the traffic rules, and panels can specify additional permissions or restrictions. Bus symbol on blue.
Lane or carriageway for scheduled public transport and other permitted users. Bus symbol on blue.
The designation shown by the crossed symbol ends. The symbol must match the preceding path or lane designation. Bus-lane symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
End of designated path or lane. Bus-lane symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
No-through roads
The road does not provide through passage. A bicycle symbol can indicate through access for bicycles and class II mopeds. A T-shaped road ends at a red block.
No through road. A T-shaped road ends at a red block.

The road does not provide through passage. A bicycle symbol can indicate through access for bicycles and class II mopeds. A bicycle symbol beyond the red block identifies through access for bicycles and class II mopeds.
No through road. A bicycle symbol beyond the red block identifies through access for bicycles and class II mopeds.
Check your understanding
Knowledge check. Is 30 km/h always appropriate on a cycle street?
Remember: Recognise the area's purpose and adapt before crossing its boundary.
Your goal: Distinguish stopping from parking and interpret the rules, signs and time panels for a proposed place.

Parking is leaving a vehicle stationary for a reason other than traffic conditions, avoiding danger, boarding or alighting, or loading or unloading goods. Remaining behind the wheel does not automatically make waiting “stopping.” Nor does switching on hazard lights create permission. Transportstyrelsen: stopping and parking
Stopping or parking restrictions Compare no parking with no stopping and parking. An extent marking needs its actual accompanying restriction; it does not create permission.
Parking is prohibited on the signed side for the applicable extent. This does not make stopping lawful where another rule prohibits it. Single red diagonal across a blue circle.
No parking. Single red diagonal across a blue circle.
Both stopping and parking are prohibited for the indicated extent. Waiting with the engine running is not a general exemption. Red cross on a blue circle.
No stopping or parking. Red cross on a blue circle.
Continue the learning
The continuous yellow edge marking indicates a stopping and parking prohibition. Continuous yellow line at the road edge.
No stopping or parking edge marking. Continuous yellow line at the road edge.
The broken yellow edge marking indicates a parking prohibition; it can also show the extent of a bus stop. Broken yellow line at the road edge.
No parking edge marking. Broken yellow line at the road edge.
This yellow marking reinforces the applicable M21 or M22 restriction. Identify which prohibition applies. Yellow zigzag marking reinforcing a stopping or parking restriction.
Reinforcement of a stopping or parking restriction. Yellow zigzag marking reinforcing a stopping or parking restriction.

Core requirements. Do not stop or park where you create danger, unnecessarily obstruct traffic or hide a sign or signal. Normally use the right side in your direction of travel; one-way roads and specified rail-track situations have exceptions. Secure the vehicle against rolling and prevent unauthorised use. Open doors only without danger or unnecessary inconvenience. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§47, 50 and 52
Continue the learning
Place
General restriction for an ordinary car
Pedestrian crossing, cycle passage or cycle crossing
No stopping on it or within 10 m before it.
Road junction
No stopping in it or within 10 m of the nearest edge of the crossing carriageway.
Crossing footway or cycle path
No stopping on it or within 10 m before it.
Tunnel, road underpass, hidden crest or obscured bend
No stopping in the prohibited location.
Beside a continuous lane boundary
No stopping if less than 3 m remains, unless a broken line lies between the car and the continuous line.
Railway level crossing
No stopping on it; no parking within 30 m on the road.
Property access
No parking in front of it or where vehicle access is substantially obstructed.
Priority road or signed passing place
No parking under the general rule; check any lawful signed provision.

Other prohibitions cover cycle lanes, hatched areas, roundabouts and lanes reserved for regular public transport. These examples are not an exhaustive catalogue of local restrictions. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§47–55
Other parking instructions Keep starts and ends paired by type. C45’s 8–18 and E30’s 30-minute conditions are separate examples, not the Tuesday two-hour exercise. Date-based parking restrictions
The parking prohibition applies on dates with an odd number. Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Single upright stroke on the no-parking symbol: odd-numbered dates.
No parking on odd-numbered dates. Single upright stroke on the no-parking symbol: odd-numbered dates.
The parking prohibition applies on dates with an even number. Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Two upright strokes on the no-parking symbol: even-numbered dates.
No parking on even-numbered dates. Two upright strokes on the no-parking symbol: even-numbered dates.
On even dates, do not park on the side with even address numbers; on odd dates, do not park on the odd-numbered side. Check any time conditions. Odd/even-date symbols divided by a red diagonal.
Date-dependent parking prohibition. Odd/even-date symbols divided by a red diagonal.
Reserved purposes and places
Read the stated purpose. A loading place concerns loading or unloading heavy or bulky goods, not unrestricted waiting. Lastplats: loading place.
Place reserved for a stated purpose. Lastplats: loading place.
The place reserved for the stated purpose ends. Loading-place symbol crossed by black lines.
End of reserved-purpose place. Loading-place symbol crossed by black lines.
This space is intended for turning and parking is prohibited. If a no-stopping symbol is inserted, stopping is prohibited too. Vändplats with a no-parking symbol.
Turning area. Vändplats with a no-parking symbol.
Continue the learning
The signed turning area ends. Turning-area sign with a no-parking symbol, crossed out.
End of turning area. Turning-area sign with a no-parking symbol, crossed out.
Read the inserted prohibition and its times together with the sign above. This panel can qualify or vary that sign; artwork variants are not interchangeable. No parking, 8–18.
Combined stopping or parking restriction. No parking, 8–18.
Zone and combined instructions
The inserted restrictions or permissions apply throughout the signed area. Locally signed exceptions do not automatically end the wider zone rule. Zone board displaying no parking.
Zone begins. Zone board displaying no parking.
Continue the learning
The zone restriction or permission shown by the matching E20 sign ends. Zone board crossed by black diagonal lines, ending no parking.
Zone ends. Zone board crossed by black diagonal lines, ending no parking.
Read the parking permission, duration and times together with the sign above. The conditions may vary the main restriction. Parking permitted for 30 minutes during 8–18.
Parking with stated conditions. Parking permitted for 30 minutes during 8–18.

At a marked bus stop, other vehicles may stop only for boarding or alighting without obstructing the relevant service. If its extent is not marked, the restricted area is normally 20 m before and 5 m after the stop sign. Loading goods is not the same exception as letting a passenger get out. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §54
Bus-stop extent The marked extent and the unmarked 20 m/5 m case are different situations. The later illustration shows the unmarked case.
This identifies a stop for scheduled services and school transport. Keep the stopping area available and watch for passengers. White bus on a blue rectangular sign.
Bus stop. White bus on a blue rectangular sign.
Continue the learning
The broken yellow edge marking indicates a parking prohibition; it can also show the extent of a bus stop. Broken yellow line at the road edge.
No parking edge marking. Broken yellow line at the road edge.

Read the whole parking instruction. On a T6 time panel, ordinary black/white times without brackets mean weekdays other than the day before a Sunday or public holiday; bracketed times mean those preceding days; red times mean Sundays and public holidays. A named day applies to that day. Check the actual date, fee, duration, vehicle group and any permit condition. A disabled-parking permit has defined benefits, not unrestricted permission to stop anywhere. Road Signs Regulation, T6–T8 and T16–T19 · Parking permits

Read each parking condition Individual reference panels, not one sign assembly. T6 and T17 contain sample times that differ from the 09–18 worked example. Do not transfer their conditions to that exercise.
Parking is permitted subject to the sign's extent, panels and other applicable restrictions. The sign does not automatically cancel general stopping and parking prohibitions. White P on blue.
Parking. White P on blue.
Continue the learning

Unbracketed black/white times apply on weekdays other than the day before a Sunday or public holiday; brackets mean those preceding days; red means Sundays and public holidays. A named day governs regardless of its category. A period crossing midnight continues into the next day.
Official time-panel example: outline 8–17, bracketed outline (8–14), and red 8–13.
Below E19, the parking instruction applies to users entitled to park with the specified accessible-parking permit. Read any time limits too. White wheelchair symbol on blue.
Accessible-parking permit holders. White wheelchair symbol on blue.
Continue the learning
The sign above applies only to the vehicle or road-user group shown on the panel. Read time qualifications as part of the same instruction.
Official outline supplementary panel containing a heavy goods vehicle symbol.
Pay according to the stated tariff and follow the other conditions at the payment facility. Read any time qualification. Text Avgift: fee.
Parking fee. Text Avgift: fee.
Indicate the start of parking with a parking disc or equivalent. Read the applicable time and duration conditions. Parking-disc symbol with 2 tim and 8–17.
Parking disc required. Parking-disc symbol with 2 tim and 8–17.
Continue the learning
This gives the longest permitted parking time. Any time panel determines when the qualification applies. 2 tim: maximum two hours.
Maximum parking duration. 2 tim: maximum two hours.
Residents with the required permit may park under the stated special conditions. Residence alone is not enough. Text Boende: resident conditions.
Resident-permit conditions. Text Boende: resident conditions.
Parking is free, but a parking ticket must be used. Do not interpret the ticket symbol as a fee requirement. Text P-biljett: parking ticket.
Free parking ticket required. Text P-biljett: parking ticket.
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned perpendicular to the panel's lower edge.
How to position the vehicle. Vehicles positioned perpendicular to the panel's lower edge.
Continue the learning
This marks a space reserved for people with mobility impairments. Check the applicable permit conditions. Wheelchair symbol painted on the road.
Accessible parking marking. Wheelchair symbol painted on the road.

On municipally maintained public places within built-up areas and within public-road areas, parking is normally limited to 24 consecutive hours on weekdays other than the day before a Sunday or public holiday. This is not a blanket rule for every private car park. Where a parking disc is required, set it to the next half-hour after arrival; if you arrive before the restricted period and remain into it, set its beginning time. Display it so it can be read. Always check the applicable signs and conditions. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §49a
Read the extent of the restriction 10 m before
Travel is left to right. No stopping on the crossing or within 10 m before it. Shading shows the rule’s extent, not a braking distance; the drawing is not to scale.
Travel is left to right. No stopping in the junction or within 10 m of the nearest edge of the crossing carriageway. Distances run from the junction edges; this schematic is not to scale.
Bus-stop sign 20 m before 5 m after

Travel is left to right. With no marked stop extent, the restriction extends 20 m before and 5 m after the stop sign. Other vehicles may stop only for boarding or alighting without obstructing the service. Shading is explanatory, not a road marking.

Worked decision. It is an ordinary Tuesday, not a holiday or the day before one. A parking sign permits at most two hours during black unbracketed 09–18. You arrive at 10:00. The two-hour restriction applies; check the other conditions before leaving the car.
The worked example’s components E19 and the two-hour T18 are shown separately here. The following exercise uses the illustrative assembly with 2 tim and black 9–18 on one plate.
Parking is permitted subject to the sign's extent, panels and other applicable restrictions. The sign does not automatically cancel general stopping and parking prohibitions. White P on blue.
Parking. White P on blue.
This gives the longest permitted parking time. Any time panel determines when the qualification applies. 2 tim: maximum two hours.
Maximum parking duration. 2 tim: maximum two hours.

Read the time conditions Try it first 2 tim 9–18 Illustrative sign combination Ordinary Tuesday, not a holiday or the day before one. In this example, parking is limited to two hours during 09–18. Arrival: 10:00. When is the two-hour limit reached, and what else must you check? Read the worked example after answering. Check your understanding
Knowledge check. Can you wait 8 m before a pedestrian crossing with the engine running?
Remember: First check whether the place is lawful at all; then check its conditions.
Your goal: Plan low-speed parking and reversing while observing changing space.

Requirements. Reverse or turn around only without danger or obstruction to other road users. Secure the parked vehicle and check before opening a door or letting passengers out. Parking inside a marked space requires the wheels to remain within its boundary. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§46, 49–50
Marked spaces and parking arrangements Each positioning panel is a separate arrangement. The marked-space boundary does not establish that a reversing path is safe.
This marks the limits of a space for a vehicle; the boundary may be broken rather than continuous. White outline of a parking space.
Parking-space boundary. White outline of a parking space.
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned perpendicular to the panel's lower edge.
How to position the vehicle. Vehicles positioned perpendicular to the panel's lower edge.
Continue the learning
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned parallel to the panel's lower edge.
How to position the vehicle. Vehicles positioned parallel to the panel's lower edge.
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned diagonally, sloping down to the right.
How to position the vehicle. Vehicles positioned diagonally, sloping down to the right.
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned diagonally, sloping down to the left.
How to position the vehicle. Vehicles positioned diagonally, sloping down to the left.

Learning approach. Select a place that offers both a safe entry and a safe departure. Check the full route of the vehicle: front corners can move sideways while you watch behind. Revisit both sides and the path ahead as the manoeuvre develops. Do not treat a camera, sensor or a helper's signal as proof that every part of the area is clear.

Stop when information is lost. If you need to inspect the area, first secure the vehicle and choose a safe way to do so. In supervised practice, learn the car's dimensions and the effect of steering gradually. A useful successful outcome is not “I parked in one movement”; it is “I kept control and did not move into uncertain space.”
Observe behind the parked vehicles
Parking bays are above the footway; the access lane is below it. The white van can hide a pedestrian from the reversing driver. No path is cleared or recommended by this drawing.

Worked decision. A delivery vehicle blocks the view of the footway behind your parking place. Rather than reversing across it in one continuous movement, you reassess the layout with your supervisor and choose a method or another place that provides the necessary view. If a pedestrian enters the path, you wait.
Check your understanding
Knowledge check. Is a pedestrian obliged to avoid your car because you began reversing first?
Remember: A small adjustment or a pause can be evidence of good judgement.
Scenario: You reach a busy neighbourhood to collect a passenger. A bus is signalling out, a cyclist is beside parked cars and the nearest space is before a crossing.
Bus detail: identify the signal and the applicable road limit before explaining your approach.
Cyclist detail: observe the parked cars, opening door and space the rider may need.
Choose a lawful collection point
Crossing detail: assess the proposed collection point. The drawing provides no measured clearance and does not label a lawful stopping place.
Explain how you will approach and choose a lawful collection point.
Keep a practice record
Record one observation that was difficult to make early, and plan a supervised exercise to improve it. Syllabus self-assessment, chapter 3 §3
